# Shared combat contracts, version 1

All behavior below is a new Youth Fighter proposal implemented incrementally; the reference client provides no evidence for these mechanics. Canonical definitions: `public/combat-data.js`. Runtime: `public/combat.js`, integrated by `world.js`. Balancing values are provisional.

## Skill and intent

The immutable registry validates unique stable IDs, path, weapon identity, role, geometry, damage formula, energy, cooldown, startup/active/recovery, ordered hit schedule, movement, interrupts/cancels, statuses, PvP scale, combo tags, unlock and presentation references. Times are simulation **seconds**, distances are map gameplay units. Paths remain `fist` and `spear`. The compatibility adapter accepts `{type:'attack',skill:0..2,pvp?:boolean}` or `{type:'attack',skillId:string,pvp?:boolean}`; if both selectors are supplied they must agree. `p.target` is selected through a target command. Unknown/wrong-path IDs, malformed selectors, incompatible equipment and ineligible targets fail without spending. Client damage, time, hit, unlock and resource fields have no effect. Runtime command shape validation applies at `YF.command`, shared by solo and host. No unbounded command queue.

## Action and lifecycle

Transient action: unique `actorId:worldActionSequence` ID, skill/target/path/map/weapon captured at start, locked facing, startAt/endAt, timings, next hit ordinal, consumed ordinal/target keys, and explicit city-attack permission. Actor position is the origin; movement is held during commitment. Map collision remains `world.move`/`maps.blocked`. No lunge is authoritative in the foundation. Fist uses unarmed hands or compatible wraps; spear has an innate designated path spear, with optional owned reed-spear bonuses. Broken durability removes the existing equipment bonus, not the path weapon. Path switching safely unequips incompatible owned weapons into the retained inventory.

Transitions: ready → startup → active → recovery → ready. Startup includes `[start, start+startup)`; active includes `[start+startup, start+startup+active)`; recovery ends at endAt. A hit at a boundary is due when `time + 1e-9 >= scheduled time`. At each outer step (finite positive dt, at most .1s), simulation splits at all action/hit/phase boundaries. Even a step crossing several boundaries consumes each hit ordinal exactly once. Equal-time actors resolve in stable player insertion order. Collision/AI movement can still differ by up to one outer simulation step; tests declare supported tolerances. Render FPS does not enter these rules.

Energy and cooldown spend together at accepted start, never at button press or impact. Interrupted or missed attacks receive **no refund**. Traveling cancels before movement between maps; arrest and defeat cancel before returning the actor; disconnect deletes the actor; restore clears transient actions, navigation, targeting and duels. Equipment and path changes cannot run during an action. A removed/dead/cross-map/protected primary causes a miss at that strike, without target substitution. The foundation does not add stagger, dodge or guard until their dependent stage.

At impact, revalidate each victim: alive, different actor, same map, not jailed, independently eligible PvP/sparring/wanted status, reach and unobstructed sampled segment (≤.08 units). Single skills affect only the primary. Foundation area parity affects the primary plus wolves/bandits within the circle, maximum eight; it never silently expands to peaceful bystanders. Every affected victim passes permission checks. Consensual sparring clamps to 1 HP and ends reciprocally. Existing law, durability, training and kill rewards run only after a confirmed eligible hit. Defeated NPCs cannot be re-hit. Later multihits require explicit per-target limits and player-return protection.

## Events and persistence

Combat event v1 includes numeric monotonically increasing `id`, stable `eventId=combat:id`, actionId, skillId, actorId, relevant targetId, mapId, simulation time and outer tick, result/phase, hitOrdinal when applicable, and position. Events are bounded to 128 entries; text events retain legacy IDs in the same sequence. Renderers deduplicate by increasing ID; a reconnect starts from the welcome sequence. Replayed snapshots never resolve hits or award resources. Events are best-effort LAN presentation, not a durable replay log; missed snapshots may lose cosmetic effects. Gameplay is in world snapshots. Never reward by consuming presentation events.

Save v4 remains compatible with v2/v3/v4 in the foundation: existing progression and sanitized city state are persistent. Action, combo, buffer, Focus and defense are transient until an explicit later contract says otherwise. Local save data is never sent at online join. Online reconnect starts a fresh session character.

## Future stages (not foundation completion claims)

Combos require authoritative outcomes, bounded buffer/window, target continuity and finite branches. Hidden techniques require teachable challenges, persistent validated unlock IDs and simulation enforcement. Focus requires real outcome caps/exclusions and reset rules. Ultimates require explicit multihit schedules, telegraph/counterplay, per-target limits and bounded enhancement. Unity can translate these contracts only after a real project compiles; no renderer or Unity project replacement is part of this work. Spatial indexing and interest management remain future scale work; queries currently filter the small same-map world.

## Implemented combo/defense stage

`combat-combos.js` defines v1 Basin Current (fist) and Reed Current (spear): confirmed primary hit 1 → confirmed primary hit 2 → hit 1 (quick) or hit 3 (heavy/area). A 1.3s window renews at each qualifying result; only the same living target/path qualifies. Wrong action/target/path, whiff, defended hit, expiry or interruption resets it. Quick final startup is 65% of ordinary startup with identical damage/cost/cooldown; heavy retains ordinary area commitment. Finish creates a 1s route lock; no infinite reopen or energy reward. River-Step Counter was deferred at this stage and is added in final integration below; Basin Current remains available for hit-confirm practice.

At most one attack intent buffers during the last 150ms of an attack commitment (including a special attack). First intent wins, expires after 150ms, stores the target ID and is revalidated at recovery end. No defense queue/cancel; no cost or cooldown bypass. Simulation boundaries include route expiry and action completion. At 20Hz this spans three nominal input steps; real LAN feel remains untuned.

Ready → defense startup → guard/dodge → recovery → ready. Q guard costs 8 energy, has .06s startup/.45s active/.18s recovery, .9s reuse lock. Facing locks toward the selected same-map target (otherwise existing facing). A source within ±70° can be guarded for 10 additional energy, receiving 40% rounded damage (minimum 1). Insufficient impact energy breaks guard and gives .2s stagger. First .12s of active guard creates .9s counter eligibility. Space dodge costs 18 energy, has .04s startup/.18s protection/.24s recovery, 1.1s reuse lock; move for the first .22s at 5 units/s along normalized intent (default backward). Protection is only the active half-open interval. Movement uses the existing swept map collision and ordinary exit/travel cancellation. Each actually avoided eligible strike creates .9s counter eligibility; harmless button spam does not. No stamina added.

Heavy confirmed hits create .12s stagger; each recipient resists subsequent staggers for 1.2s. Stagger cancels attack/defense/buffer/combo and holds movement until recovery, then defense is available subject to its existing reuse lock. Defeat/travel/arrest outrank stagger; guard/dodge resolve before damage. No ordinary cancel into defense during commitment. Non-guard enemies now approach, hold a .4s locked directional anticipation, revalidate distance ≤1.8, map, target life and obstruction, strike once, then hold .4s recovery. Guards retain their pursuit/crime attack rhythm and their damage passes through the same player defense resolution.

Spear ordinary attacks now use locked cones: thrust ±.35 rad (one primary target), sweep ±.6π, tempest ±.4π. This is an intentional positioning change from foundation radial parity. Origin remains the stationary actor. HUD status and anticipation polygons are procedural, original, read-only and visible with reduced decorative effects. Defense uses explicit pose handling; spear remains visible throughout. Authored defense sprite frames and recorded martial sound assets are unavailable: existing pose columns and procedural tones are placeholders.

## Implemented discovery and save v5

`combat-discovery.js` owns a three-minute transient challenge offered only by the nearby living Temple trainer while lawful and ready. Complete a confirmed route on temple-dummy; then request Practice pulse within three units. Each request has a two-second reuse lock and a visible .6-second anticipation; the nonlethal four-damage pulse revalidates source, map, distance ≤3.5 and obstruction. An active dodge or early guard (the actual timed result of this strike) discovers the current path's technique. Missing/late defense can be retried. Neither client flags nor mere input order establish proof. Challenge/drill clear on path change, travel, arrest, defeat, expiry or load.

Hidden IDs: `fist.basin-echo` and `spear.tide-reversal`. Both require a known persistent unlock and a .9s opportunity earned by actually defending a strike. Activation consumes the opportunity, spends 16/20 energy respectively and starts an eight-second independent cooldown. Basin Echo: single target, 2.8 reach, 26 damage, .12/.1/.28 timing, on confirmed hit opens a .9s quick-basic follow-up at 65% startup with unchanged damage. Tide-Reversal Spear: 4.2 reach front sweep, 24 damage, .22/.1/.28 timing. Spear identity stays consistent. There is no passive damage increase and ordinary viability does not depend on discovery.

Save snapshot is now version **5** and restores **2/3/4/5**. `combatProgress={version:1,unlocks:[known stable IDs]}` is sanitized against the registry, and independent cooldowns are clamped to each known technique's maximum. Older saves start with no hidden unlocks and retain their prior progress and compatible equipment. Actions, queued intent, route/challenge/drill, counter/follow-up opportunities, defense locks and stagger proofs never persist. Solo storage key remains unchanged. Network join accepts none of this data.

## Implemented Focus and ultimates

`combat-focus.js` bounds transient Mastery Focus to 0–100. Award once per accepted action: 4 for a confirmed damaging hit against a living same-map wolf/bandit, plus 8 for a completed hostile route; a timed hostile defense gives 6, once per defense action. All awards share a 30-point rolling ten-second global cap and a 20-point rolling thirty-second per-enemy cap. Ledger entries are bounded to 64 and pruned; ultimate hits give no Focus. Training dummies, practice pulses, civilians, guards, all player combat/sparring and harmless inputs give none. Actual simulation outcomes call the award functions directly; presentation/replayed events do not. Focus and the enhancement opportunity reset to zero on travel, actual path change, arrest/defeat, load or reconnect. Focus is excluded from saves and joining with forged Focus has no effect. Ordinary interruptions retain unspent Focus; any accepted ultimate spends without refund, including a miss or interruption.

New IDs: `fist.golden-basin-resonance` (Golden Basin Resonance) and `spear.river-crown-tempest` (River Crown Tempest). Both are stationary commitments requiring 60 Focus + 30 energy and a separate 30s cooldown. No hidden discovery is required. Existing third skills remain ordinary 45-energy/9s attacks. Basic damage uses the existing formula. Scheduled special strikes apply `max(1,(base + levelBonus + equipmentAttack)*hitScale - equipmentDefence)` before guard adjustment; floating HP is supported and displayed damage is rounded for readability.

Resonance: .65s startup, .35s active, .45s recovery; pulse at .65s with reach 2.5 / 45% of 54 base damage, then .85s with reach 4.5 / 55%. Maximum two hits per victim, eight victims per ordinal. Tempest: .6s startup, .7s active, .45s recovery; strikes at .6/.8/1.0s each deal 20% of 64 base damage in a locked ±.28 rad cone to one target; the 1.2s finish deals 40% in ±.55 rad, maximum four targets. Reach six, maximum four hits per victim. Each intended ordinal/target pair is consumed once, including a defended attempt. A defeated/returned player or completed sparring victim is excluded for the rest of the action. Primary removal/death/protection/map/range/geometry is revalidated at every ordinal; no silent target replacement.

Spacing out of reach/cone, timed defense and a heavy startup interruption supply counterplay. All rays and movement stay in gameplay space and use map collision. Anticipation stays visible with reduced decorative effects; there is no cinematic lock or camera takeover. Presentation uses explicit existing pose mappings and original procedural geometry, with authored ultimate animation/audio still missing.

Hostile route completion creates a two-second same-target/path enhancement opportunity. Explicit `{enhanced:true}` costs **70 Focus + 35 energy**, keeps the 30s cooldown and multiplies only the final ordinal by **1.15**. It adds no hits, guarantees or Focus. Expired/mismatched claims reject without cost; accepted activation consumes the opportunity. Travel, path change, defeat and interruptions clear it. Keys: 5 standard; V enhanced; button state describes current requirements. The rate caps and all timings are provisional until actual browser/LAN practice.


## Final integration: River-Step Counter and compatibility

Now that defense is tested, Fist also implements `fist.river-step-counter`: actually dodge an eligible incoming strike during protection (practice dummies excluded), then confirm Elbow Surge against that same attacker and finish with 1 quick or 3 heavy. It shares the 1.3s link windows, finite branches and 1s route lock. Dodging harmlessly does not create it. Changing target, whiffing, expiry or interruption resets it. The hidden response remains an alternative use of the separate .9s counter opportunity. Both the ordinary hit-confirm route and the counter route remain available; mentor discovery uses the ordinary route on the dummy.

Runtime intent validation preserves the existing city UI nullable npc/peer fields while still checking consumed IDs and amounts in the service authority. Actual travel/load clear stale stagger and route locks. Focus/action events remain session-scoped, best-effort presentation IDs, not durable account/replay identifiers. Heavy stagger status is declared in the registry and interpreted by the shared hit resolver.
